I did a raw food diet for 2 weeks and while I clearly got enough calories, I was perpetually hungry.

Everything I ate was, essentially, salad. My SO and I at the time did allow ourselves to 'cheat' by having salmon jerky even though it was probably heated above 140F at some point.

It was brutal. If you ever want to screw around with your biochemical processes, try only eating raw food for one week. I did two. One is enough to get the idea.

Greens and veggies are fine, fruit is fine, raw fish is fine (but no rice or soy sauce) and raw (not roasted) nuts are fine.

That's pretty much it. No bread, no rice, no beans, no proper meat.

I'm glad I did it just to see what it was like but it's seriously jarring as hell.

You will shit huge clean turds in 15 seconds. By day 5 you will be full of energy and require less sleep.

Your waking life, however, is quite miserable. You are hungry when you wake up. You are hungry when you go to sleep. You are hungry about an hour after you eat.

Day 3 is the worst. You'll feel sick as a dog as your body starts shifting priorities to accommodate this retarded experiment.

And when you come out of it a week or two later, it's really difficult to stomach meat and beer and bread and all the other things that make life worth living.

Final Fantasy XI did this over 10 years ago. The game launched on PS2 in Japan in 2002 and later that year became available in North America on PC. It was later also released on PS2 and eventually XBox 360 in North America and in a number of other places around the world. Players all played on the same dedicated servers regardless of which platform they were using.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final_Fantasy_XI

Wow i didn't expecting it to be happening that long ago, i've heard of a lot of games wanting to do it for a while but never heard of any that followed thru. For whatever reason, Final Fantasy is a series i just never played.

When Final Fantasy XI was released on PS2 in North America, the retail box you bought included a hard drive for the PS2 which was a fairly common add-on in Japan but had never been available in North America. It was necessary to accommodate the ongoing patches and additions that were made to the game, as with most MMORPGs. I think FFXI might remain the only console game to ever ship with a hard drive. Beyond that, the main things that had to be overcome were making sure the console controls were viable and providing a means for console players without a keyboard to be able to communicate with other players at a time where integrated voice chat wasn't an option. They did a pretty decent job of it for the time but most developers would have given up at the lack of a hard drive on the PS2.
